title: Developing and validating a high-throughput robotic system for the accelerated development of porous membranes

metadata.authors: H. Wang; S. Zeinali Danalou; J. Zhu; K. Sulimro; C. Lim; S. Basak; A. Tai; U. Siriwardana; J. Hattrick-Simpers; J. R. Werber

source_summary: This study introduces a fully automated, modular platform for fabricating and characterizing porous polymeric membranes via nonsolvent-induced phase separation, enabling precise, reproducible, and high-throughput experimentation with integrated mechanical testing to support data-driven membrane optimization.
abstract: The development of porous polymeric membranes remains a labor-intensive process, often requiring extensive trial and error to identify optimal fabrication parameters. In this study, we present a fully automated platform for membrane fabrication and characterization via nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS). The system integrates automated solution preparation, blade casting, controlled immersion, and compression testing, allowing precise control over fabrication parameters such as polymer concentration and ambient humidity. The modular design enables reproducible sample handling to improve consistency and can be adapted for future parallel processing to further reduce experimental time. Compression testing is introduced as a sensitive mechanical characterization method for estimating membrane stiffness and as a proxy to infer porosity and intra-sample uniformity through automated analysis of stress–strain curves. As a proof of concept to demonstrate the effectiveness of the system, NIPS was carried out with polysulfone, the green solvent PolarClean®, and water as the polymer, solvent, and nonsolvent, respectively. Experiments conducted with the automated system reproduced expected effects of polymer concentration and ambient humidity on membrane properties, namely increased stiffness and uniformity with increasing polymer concentration and humidity variations in pore morphology and mechanical response. The developed automated platform supports high-throughput experimentation and is well-suited for integration into self-driving laboratory workflows, offering a scalable and reproducible foundation for data-driven optimization of porous polymeric membranes through NIPS. © 2025 The Authors.
